questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Labour is defined as the process by which a fetus, after attaining ______, is expelled from the ______.
opts: Period of viability; genital tract
Term; uterus
28 weeks; birth canal
Lung maturity; pelvis
questions.exp: Labour = process by which a fetus after attaining the period of viability is expelled from the genital tract. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: All of the following are among the five criteria for normal labour EXCEPT:
opts: Delivery by caesarean section if the labour becomes prolonged
Spontaneous onset of the labour
Term gestation, that is 37 to 42 completed weeks
Vertex presentation with an uncomplicated vaginal delivery
questions.exp: The five criteria are spontaneous onset, term gestation (37-42 weeks), vertex presentation, uncomplicated delivery and vaginal delivery. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Match the phase of parturition with what characterises it — 1) Phase 1, uterine quiescence 2) Phase 2, myometrial activation 3) Phase 4 … A) The postpartum phase B) Unresponsive uterus, soft cervix, progesterone the main hormone C) Functional progesterone withdrawal with cervical ripening
questions.exp: Phase 1 is quiescence with an unresponsive uterus, soft cervix and progesterone dominant; phase 2 is activation with functional progesterone withdrawal, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening; phase 4 is the postpartum phase. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: All of the following occur in phase 2 of parturition, the myometrial activation phase, EXCEPT:
opts: A rise in progesterone action
Functional withdrawal of progesterone with a rise in estrogen
More oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors with more gap junctions
Ripening of the cervix
questions.exp: Phase 2 is functional withdrawal of progesterone, a rise in estrogen, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening — not a rise in progesterone action. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Match phase 3 and phase 4 of labour:
opts: Phase 3 = uterine stimulation/contraction (all stages of labour); Phase 4 = postpartum phase
Phase 3 = quiescence; Phase 4 = activation
Phase 3 = postpartum; Phase 4 = involution
Phase 3 = cervical ripening; Phase 4 = delivery
questions.exp: Phase 3: uterine stimulation – all stages of labour included; Phase 4: postpartum. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
questions.q: Fill up: The fetal cascade for the onset of labour runs from fetal hypothalamic ______ to pituitary ACTH to fetal adrenal ______ and then to placental estrogen.
opts: CRH; DHEA-S
ACTH; cortisol
CRH; progesterone
Oxytocin; DHEA-S
questions.exp: The cascade is hypothalamic CRH, pituitary ACTH, fetal adrenal DHEA-sulfate, conversion to estrogen in the placenta and then uterine contractions. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Definition, criteria & phases of labour
questions.q: Fill up: Labour is defined by painful uterine contractions that produce progressive ______ and ______ of the cervix.
opts: effacement; dilatation
rupture; descent
descent; expulsion
softening; shortening of the lower segment
questions.exp: Contractions alone are not enough; the cervix must show progressive effacement and dilatation for the diagnosis of true labour. (Book p512)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Fill up: Lightening is descent of the fetal head into the pelvis, which causes a ______ in fundal height and relieves ______.
opts: Fall; respiratory distress
Rise; respiratory distress
Fall; ankle edema
Rise; gastric reflux
questions.exp: Lightening is descent of the head into the pelvis, lowering the fundal height and relieving respiratory distress. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Which statement about cervical ripening before labour is TRUE?
opts: Ripening reduces cross-linking of fibres and raises water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases cross-linking and reduces water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases collagen deposition and reduces the water content
Ripening increases elastin and reduces the amount of hyaluronic acid
questions.exp: Ripening is due to prostaglandins and connective-tissue change: less cross-linking of fibres, more water content and more hyaluronic acid. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Which statement about true versus false labour pain is TRUE?
opts: True labour contractions are regular and progressive in strength; false labour pains are neither
True labour contractions are irregular and continuous; false labour pains are regular and rhythmic
True labour contractions continue at a fixed intensity; false labour pains are rhythmic and progressive
True labour contractions are regular but decreasing; false labour pains are progressive and rhythmic
questions.exp: True labour contractions are regular and increase in frequency, duration and intensity; false labour pains do neither. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Match the feature of labour with the type of labour it belongs to — 1) Site of the pain 2) Show and bag of membranes 3) Response to sedation, enema and rest … A) Relieved by sedation in false labour, not relieved in true labour B) Lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh in true labour C) Show present and membranes felt in true labour
questions.exp: True labour pain is in the lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh, the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt, and it is not relieved by sedation; false labour does not radiate, has no show, and is relieved by sedation, enema and rest. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Fill up: In true labour the show is ______ and the bag of membranes ______; in false labour neither is found.
opts: Present; is felt
Absent; is felt
Present; is not felt
Absent; is not felt
questions.exp: In true labour the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt; in false labour the show is absent and the membranes are not felt. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Fill up: False labour pains are ______ by sedation, enema and rest, whereas true labour pains are ______.
opts: Relieved; not relieved
Not relieved; relieved
Relieved; relieved as well
Unchanged; relieved only by analgesia
questions.exp: False labour pains respond to sedation, enema and rest; true labour pains do not. (Book p513)

questions.sec: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
questions.q: Match the pattern with its meaning — 1) True labour 2) False labour 3) Pre-labour or prodromal phase … A) Irregular contractions that do not intensify and settle with rest or sedation B) Regular contractions increasing in frequency and intensity with cervical change C) Cervical ripening with a show and irregular pains before active labour begins
questions.exp: False labour settles with rest and does not change the cervix; the prodromal phase is the uncomfortable run-up to real labour. (Book p513)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Fill up: The three Ps required for labour are ______, ______ and ______.
opts: Push (contractions), Passage (pelvis), Passenger (baby)
Pain, Pelvis, Placenta
Position, Presentation, Power
Progesterone, Prostaglandin, Pitocin
questions.exp: The 3 Ps are Push, meaning uterine contractions, Passage, meaning the pelvis, and Passenger, meaning the baby. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Match each feature of uterine contractions with its value — 1) Origin 2) Speed of spread 3) Time to depolarise the whole uterus 4) Predominant site … A) 2 cm per second B) Fundus C) Cornua D) 15 seconds
questions.exp: Contractions originate in the cornua, spread at 2 cm per second, take 15 seconds to depolarise the entire uterus, and are predominant at the fundus. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Fill up: Palpable ______ mmHg, painful 15 mmHg, cervical dilatation 20–25 mmHg.
opts: 10 mmHg; 15 mmHg; 20–25 mmHg
15 mmHg; 10 mmHg; 40 mmHg
20 mmHg; 25 mmHg; 50 mmHg
5 mmHg; 10 mmHg; 15 mmHg
questions.exp: Palpable 10 mmHg, painful 15 mmHg, cervical dilatation 20–25 mmHg. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: A 28-year-old second gravida at 12 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions. According to the notes, 1st stage 40–50 mmHg; 2nd/3rd stage 100–120 mmHg; basal tone 10–20 mmHg; monitored every 30 min. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
opts: Advise that 40–50 mmhg : 100–120 mmhg : 10–20 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 100–120 : 40–50 : 5 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 20–25 : 40–50 : 10 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 60–75 : 120–150 : 20–30 is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
questions.exp: 1st stage 40–50 mmHg; 2nd/3rd stage 100–120 mmHg; basal tone 10–20 mmHg; monitored every 30 min. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Fill up: 1 MVU = ______ (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min; adequate = 200–220 MVU.
opts: Strength of contraction (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min
Duration (sec) × number in 10 min
Strength (mmHg) ÷ duration
Number of contractions per hour × 10
questions.exp: 1 MVU = strength (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min; adequate = 200–220 MVU. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Fill up: Upper segment = ______ uterus (contracts); lower segment = isthmus (passively dilates); effaced cervix becomes part of LUS. Blood flow to uterus ↓ during contractions.
opts: Entire uterus; contracts; isthmus; passively dilates; lower uterine segment
Isthmus; dilates; fundus; contracts; upper segment
Fundus; relaxes; cervix; contracts; vagina
Corpus; dilates; isthmus; contracts; fundus
questions.exp: Upper segment = entire uterus (contracts); lower segment = isthmus (passively dilates); effaced cervix becomes part of LUS. Blood flow to uterus ↓ during contractions. (Book p514)

questions.sec: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
questions.q: Fill up: The three Ps that determine the outcome of labour are ______.
opts: powers, passenger and passage
powers, placenta and pelvis
pressure, position and placenta
powers, prostaglandins and progesterone
questions.exp: Uterine powers, the fetus as passenger and the maternal bony passage together decide whether labour will be normal or obstructed. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Fill up: Tachysystole = ______/10 min; m/c cause misoprostol > oxytocin.
opts: >5 contractions in 10 min; misoprostol (> oxytocin)
>3 in 10 min; oxytocin
Contractions >60 sec; dinoprostone
>7 in 10 min; Foley catheter
questions.exp: Tachysystole = >5 contractions/10 min; m/c cause misoprostol > oxytocin. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Match the tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions with the correct detail — 1) The consequence of tachysystole and its CTG picture 2) Management sequence of tachysystole: 3) Precipitate labour is defined as completion of the … A) Fetal distress due to ↓ blood supply; prolonged deceleration B) Stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, give oxygen, fluids if needed, then terbutaline C) <3 hours; perineal tear, hematoma, PPH
questions.exp: Consequence: fetal distress (↓ blood supply); CTG shows prolonged deceleration. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: All of the following are Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions — Management sequence of tachysystole: EXCEPT:
opts: Fetal distress due to ↓ blood supply; prolonged deceleration
>5 contractions in 10 min; misoprostol (> oxytocin)
Push (contractions), Passage (pelvis), Passenger (baby)
Stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, give oxygen, fluids if needed, then terbutaline
questions.exp: Tachysystole is managed by stopping the oxytocin, repositioning, oxygen and fluids, with a tocolytic such as terbutaline if it persists. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: Fill up: Precipitate labour: entire process ______ h → perineal tear, hematoma, PPH.
opts: <3 hours; perineal tear, hematoma, PPH
<1 hour; uterine inversion only
<6 hours; retained placenta
<12 hours; fetal distress
questions.exp: Precipitate labour: entire process <3 h → perineal tear, hematoma, PPH. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: A 30-year-old G3P1L1 at 12 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions. According to the notes, hypotonic contractions lead to prolonged or slow progress of labour and are managed by augmentation with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
opts: Advise that prolonged slow progress of labour; augmentation with arm and oxytocin is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that fetal distress from reduced perfusion; tocolysis with terbutaline is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that precipitate labour with rapid delivery; tocolysis and bed rest is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that uterine rupture with severe pain; immediate caesarean section is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
questions.exp: Hypotonic contractions lead to prolonged or slow progress of labour and are managed by augmentation with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
questions.q: All of the following are features of precipitate labour EXCEPT:
opts: A latent phase lasting more than twenty hours
Delivery completed within about three hours of the first contraction
A higher risk of cervical, vaginal and perineal lacerations
A higher risk of postpartum haemorrhage from uterine atony
questions.exp: Precipitate labour is abnormally fast, so it tears the birth canal and leaves an exhausted uterus; a long latent phase is its opposite. (Book p514)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Which statement about Augmentation of labour — Kocher s forceps is TRUE?
opts: Kocher's forceps, with a single tooth, rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Allis forceps, which are identified by several fine teeth on the jaws is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
A sponge holder, which is identified by its smooth, atraumatic jaws is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
An amnihook, which is identified by its single plastic hook is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: Kocher's forceps has a single tooth at the tip with rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations on the jaws. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Fill up: Rupture of membranes releases ______ which augments labour.
opts: PGE2
Oxytocin
PGF2α
Estrogen
questions.exp: Rupture of membranes releases PGE2 which augments labour. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Match the augmentation of labour with the correct detail — 1) Absolute contraindications to ARM are: 2) In abruptio placentae, ARM is beneficial because it: 3) Indication for augmentation is slow progress (dilatation <1 … A) Maternal HIV, genital herpes infection, IUD of fetus B) Confirms the diagnosis and accelerates the process of labour C) Engaged: ARM → 30 min → oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ cord prolapse risk)
questions.exp: Absolute C/I: maternal HIV, genital herpes, IUD of fetus. Relative: polyhydramnios (↑ abruption risk) – controlled rupture with slow release. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Which statement about Augmentation of labour — ARM in abruptio is TRUE?
opts: Confirms the diagnosis and accelerates the process of labour is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Stops the bleeding by tamponade is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Reduces risk of DIC directly is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Allows external cephalic version is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: ARM in abruptio placenta confirms diagnosis and accelerates labour. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: Which statement about Augmentation of labour — Head engaged ARM is TRUE?
opts: Engaged: ARM → 30 min → oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ cord prolapse risk) is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Engaged: oxytocin → ARM; not engaged: ARM → oxytocin is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Both: ARM immediately followed by oxytocin is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Both: oxytocin only is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: Head engaged: ARM then oxytocin after 30 min; head not engaged: oxytocin first, then ARM to avoid cord prolapse. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
questions.q: A primigravida at 4 cm has contractions every six minutes lasting 25 seconds, with no cervical change over four hours, intact membranes and a normal CTG. What is the next step?
opts: Amniotomy, reassess progress, then add oxytocin if contractions stay inadequate
Immediate caesarean section for failure to progress
Sedation and rest for twelve hours before any reassessment
Discharge home, because she cannot be in labour without cervical change
questions.exp: Inadequate contractions with intact membranes are augmented by amniotomy first, with oxytocin added only if contractions remain poor. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Engagement descent flexion is TRUE?
opts: Engagement → descent → flexion → internal rotation & crowning → extension → external rotation (restitution) → expulsion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Descent → engagement → extension → flexion → internal rotation → expulsion → restitution is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Engagement → flexion → descent → extension → internal rotation → restitution → expulsion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Flexion → engagement → descent → crowning → internal rotation → expulsion → extension is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: Engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation & crowning, extension, external rotation (restitution), expulsion. (Book p515)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Normal delivery longitudinal is TRUE?
opts: Longitudinal; cephalic; vertex is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Longitudinal; breech; sacrum is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Oblique; cephalic; brow is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Transverse; shoulder; acromion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: Normal delivery: longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, vertex presenting part; head usually in LOT (LOT > LOA). (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: A 32-year-old primigravida at 9 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding cardinal movements & the process of labour. According to the notes, occiput rotates 2/8th of a circle (90°) at the ischial spine level: 45° by neck + 45° by shoulders. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
opts: Advise that 2/8th; ischial spine; 45°; 45° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 1/8th; ischial tuberosity; 45°; 0° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 3/8th; pelvic brim; 90°; 45° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 2/8th; pelvic outlet; 60°; 30° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
questions.exp: Occiput rotates 2/8th of a circle (90°) at the ischial spine level: 45° by neck + 45° by shoulders. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: A 26-year-old primigravida at 9 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding cardinal movements & the process of labour. According to the notes, crowning is the head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions, with episiotomy only if required. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
opts: Advise that head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions, episiotomy only if needed is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that head visible at the labia only during a contraction is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that descent of the head down onto the pelvic levator ani muscle is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that delivery of the head by extension over the stretched perineum is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
questions.exp: Crowning is the head seen at the labia irrespective of contractions, with episiotomy only if required. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Restitution untwists neck is TRUE?
opts: Restitution: the neck untwists after delivery — external rotation: the shoulders turn one eighth of a circle is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: the shoulders rotate one eighth — external rotation: the neck untwists is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: the head extends as it is born — external rotation: the head flexes back is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: descent through the cavity — external rotation: expulsion of the body is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: Restitution untwists the neck after internal rotation, and external rotation then aligns the shoulders with the antero-posterior diameter. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — WHO recommends perineal is TRUE?
opts: Perineal massage, warm towel, support the perineum, flex then extend the head is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Routine episiotomy, fundal pressure, and early maternal pushing efforts is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Lithotomy position, the Kristeller manoeuvre, and perineal shaving is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Vacuum extraction, perineal shaving, and routine episiotomy in all is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
questions.exp: WHO recommends perineal massage, a warm towel at the perineum, supporting the perineum with the hand, and flexing the head initially then extending it for delivery. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
questions.q: Match the cardinal movement with its description — 1) Engagement 2) Internal rotation 3) Extension … A) The occiput rotates anteriorly through about 45 degrees to lie behind the symphysis pubis B) The head is born by extending as it pivots under the symphysis pubis C) The biparietal diameter passes through the plane of the pelvic inlet
questions.exp: The sequence is engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, then restitution, external rotation and expulsion. (Book p516)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Engagement is defined as the ______ crossing the ______; it occurs at ______ in primigravida and ______ in multigravida.
opts: Largest transverse diameter (biparietal) of head; pelvic inlet; 38 wks; time of labour
Sub-occipito-bregmatic; pelvic outlet; 36 wks; 38 wks
Occipito-frontal; mid-pelvis; 40 wks; 40 wks
Bitemporal; brim; labour; 38 wks
questions.exp: Engagement = biparietal diameter crosses pelvic inlet; primi 38 wks, multi at labour. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Signs of engagement – on P/A : on P/V.
opts: ≤2/5th of head palpable : 0 station
5/5th palpable : −2 station
3/5th palpable : +2 station
Non-ballotable : −3 station
questions.exp: P/A ≤2/5 palpable; P/V station 0. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Causes of non-engagement in a primigravida at term, in order of frequency:
opts: Deflexed head, then CPD, then placenta previa, then polyhydramnios
CPD, then placenta previa, then a deflexed head, then polyhydramnios
Placenta previa, then polyhydramnios, then CPD, then a deflexed head
Wrong dates, then a deflexed head, then CPD, then placenta previa
questions.exp: Causes of non-engagement in a primigravida at term, in order of frequency, are a deflexed head (commonest), then CPD, then placenta previa; others are polyhydramnios and wrong dates. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Before P/V examination in a primigravida with a free-floating head, ______ must be ruled out; engagement rules out ______.
opts: Placenta previa; CPD at the level of inlet
Cord prolapse; malposition
Abruption; contracted outlet
Vasa previa; deflexion
questions.exp: Rule out placenta previa before P/V in primigravida with free floating head; engagement rules out CPD at the inlet. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
questions.q: Match degree of flexion → presenting part → engaging AP diameter: Fully flexed : Deflexed : Partially extended : Fully extended.
opts: Vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic : vertex/occipito-frontal 11.5 cm : brow/mento-vertical → C-section : face/submento-vertical & submento-bregmatic
Vertex/occipito-frontal : brow/mento-vertical : face/submento-bregmatic : vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic
Face/submento-bregmatic : vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic : brow/mento-vertical : vertex/occipito-frontal
Brow/mento-vertical : vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic : face/submento-vertical : vertex/occipito-frontal
questions.exp: Fully flexed vertex – sub-occipitobregmatic; deflexed vertex – occipito-frontal 11.5 cm; brow – mento-vertical (C-section); face – submento-vertical/submento-bregmatic. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Engagement: definition, signs & engaging diameters
questions.q: Fill up: The head is engaged when the ______ has passed through the pelvic inlet, after which only ______ of the head is palpable abdominally.
opts: biparietal diameter; two-fifths or less
suboccipito-bregmatic diameter; three-fifths
biparietal diameter; four-fifths
occipito-frontal diameter; none at all
questions.exp: With the biparietal diameter through the brim, the sinciput is the only part easily felt above the symphysis. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: Synclitic engagement means the sagittal suture lies in the transverse diameter of the pelvis:
opts: Midway between the pubic symphysis and the sacral promontory
Closer to the pubic symphysis than to the sacral promontory
Closer to the sacral promontory than to the pubic symphysis
In the anteroposterior diameter, not the transverse diameter
questions.exp: Synclitic engagement means the sagittal suture lies in the transverse diameter midway between the pubic symphysis and the sacral promontory (LOT position). (Book p517)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: Which of the following statements about asynclitism is TRUE?
opts: The sagittal suture is deflected towards the sacrum or the symphysis so that one parietal bone leads, and mild degrees usually correct with good contractions
Asynclitism means the head is deflexed, so that the brow presents instead of the vertex
Every case of asynclitism needs caesarean section, since the head cannot negotiate the pelvis
In anterior asynclitism the posterior parietal bone always presents and always obstructs labour
questions.exp: Anterior asynclitism is Naegele obliquity and posterior is Litzmann obliquity; both usually correct with effective contractions and decent pelvis. (Book p517)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: In ANTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards the ______, giving a ______ presentation, with ______ prognosis.
opts: Sacrum; anterior parietal; better
Pubic symphysis; posterior parietal; worse
Sacrum; posterior parietal; worse
Pubic symphysis; anterior parietal; better
questions.exp: Anterior asynclitism: sagittal suture towards sacrum, anterior parietal presentation, better prognosis. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: In POSTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards ______ and the presentation is ______.
opts: Pubic symphysis; posterior parietal
Sacrum; anterior parietal
Pubic symphysis; anterior parietal
Ischial spine; occipital
questions.exp: Posterior asynclitism: suture deflected towards pubic symphysis, posterior parietal presentation. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
questions.q: The head of the baby is delivered by ______ in vertex and by ______ in breech/face.
opts: Extension; flexion
Flexion; extension
Rotation; extension
Extension; extension
questions.exp: Vertex – head delivered by extension; breech/face – by flexion. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Pain during the 1st stage arises from ______ (T10–L1) plus ______ (S2–S4).
opts: Uterine contractions; dilatation of cervix
Perineal stretching; cervical dilatation
Uterine contractions; perineal stretching
Round ligament; bladder
questions.exp: 1st stage: uterine contractions (T10–L1) + cervical dilatation (S2–S4). (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Pain during the 2nd stage is from cervical dilatation (S2–S4) plus stretching of the perineum via the ______ nerve (______).
opts: Pudendal; S2–S4
Ilioinguinal; L1
Genitofemoral; L1–L2
Obturator; L2–L4
questions.exp: 2nd stage: cervical dilatation S2–S4 + perineal stretch via pudendal nerve (S2–S4). (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Epidural analgesia in labour – level of block : type of block.
opts: T10 level; sensory and sympathetic block without motor block
T4 level; motor and sensory block without sympathetic block
L1 level; sympathetic block only, with no sensory block
S2 level; dense motor block with no sensory or sympathetic block
questions.exp: Epidural analgesia in labour aims at a T10 level with sensory and sympathetic block but no motor block. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Drugs of choice for labour epidural and its effect on stages of labour:
opts: Bupivacaine 0.625% or ropivacaine; shortens the 1st stage, prolongs the 2nd by 1 hour
Bupivacaine 0.5%; shortens both the 1st and the 2nd stage of labour
Lignocaine 2%; prolongs both the 1st and the 2nd stage of labour
Ropivacaine alone; no measurable effect on any stage of labour
questions.exp: The drugs of choice for labour epidural are bupivacaine 0.625% or ropivacaine; it shortens the first stage and prolongs the second stage by about 1 hour. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Contraindication to epidural and the fact about C-section rate:
opts: Anticoagulant in the 12-24 hours before labour; it does not raise the caesarean rate
Hypertension in labour; epidural doubles the caesarean section rate
Multiparity; epidural increases the forceps rate but not caesarean
Diabetes in pregnancy; epidural reduces the caesarean section rate
questions.exp: Epidural is contraindicated by anticoagulant use in the 12-24 hours before the onset of labour, and it does not increase the caesarean section rate. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
questions.q: Fill up: First-stage labour pain is visceral and enters the cord at ______, while second-stage somatic perineal pain travels mainly in ______.
opts: T10 to L1; the pudendal nerve (S2 to S4)
S2 to S4; T10 to L1
T6 to T8; the femoral nerve
L1 to L2; the obturator nerve
questions.exp: This is why an epidural covering T10 to L1 relieves contraction pain and a pudendal or low block is enough for the second stage. (Book p518)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Pudendal nerve block – site : ligament pierced : stage of pain relieved.
opts: Ischial spine : sacrospinous ligament : 2nd stage
Ischial tuberosity : sacrotuberous ligament : 1st stage
Ischial spine : sacrotuberous : 1st stage
Pubic tubercle : inguinal ligament : 3rd stage
questions.exp: Pudendal block at ischial spine, piercing sacrospinous ligament, relieves 2nd stage pain. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses of pudendal block are ______; it does NOT block pain during ______.
opts: Instrumental delivery and perineal or vaginal tear repair; cervical tears
Caesarean section and manual removal of the placenta; episiotomy
Repair of cervical tears; repair of the perineum afterwards
Suction evacuation of the uterus; instrumental delivery in labour
questions.exp: Pudendal block is used for instrumental delivery and repair of perineal or vaginal tears, but it does not block pain during repair of cervical tears. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Paracervical block – sites : sites avoided (and why) : duration.
opts: 2 or 4 o'clock and 8 or 10 o'clock : 3 and 9 o'clock (descending cervical artery) : 1–2 hrs
3 and 9 o'clock : 12 and 6 o'clock (urethra/rectum) : 4 hrs
12 and 6 o'clock : 3 and 9 (uterine artery) : 30 min
5 and 7 o'clock : 2 and 10 : 6 hrs
questions.exp: Sites 2/4 and 8/10 o'clock; avoid 3 and 9 o'clock because of the descending cervical artery; lasts 1–2 h. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses and contraindication of paracervical block:
opts: Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in labour (fetal bradycardia)
Instrumental delivery and perineal repair; contraindicated in labour (bradycardia)
Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in hypertension
Caesarean section and suturing; contraindicated in multiple pregnancy
questions.exp: Paracervical block is used for repair of the cervix and for suction and evacuation, but is contraindicated in labour because it causes fetal bradycardia. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Prostaglandins act on ______ receptors present on ______ and are released ______.
opts: G-protein cell membrane; myometrium and cervix; locally (paracrine)
Nuclear; endometrium; systemically (endocrine)
Tyrosine kinase; cervix only; locally
Ion channel; decidua; endocrine
questions.exp: G-protein coupled membrane receptors on myometrium and cervix; local paracrine release. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Match prostaglandin synthesis site to product and action – Decidua & myometrium : Amnion.
opts: PGF2α (uterine action) : PGE2 (acts on cervix)
PGE2 (cervix) : PGF2α (uterus)
PGI2 : thromboxane
PGE1 : PGF2α
questions.exp: Decidua/myometrium → PGF2α (uterine action); amnion → PGE2 (cervical action). (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: Uses of prostaglandins in obstetrics include induction (sweeping fingers in internal os releases PGE2 → cervical ripening), and:
opts: Augmentation of labour and management of PPH
Tocolysis and cervical cerclage
Treatment of pre-eclampsia
Prevention of preterm labour
questions.exp: Uses: induction, augmentation of labour, management of PPH. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
questions.q: All of the following statements about pudendal nerve block are true EXCEPT:
opts: It abolishes the pain of uterine contractions in the first stage
It is given transvaginally with the needle directed just below the ischial spine
It provides perineal analgesia for an instrumental delivery
It does not relieve the pain of the contracting uterus
questions.exp: Pudendal block anaesthetises the perineum only; first-stage visceral pain needs a paracervical block or regional analgesia. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Induction of labour (IOL) is defined as ______; Bishop score checks ______ with a maximum of ______.
opts: Initiation of uterine contractions in a patient not in labour; readiness of cervix and uterus before IOL; 13
Acceleration of established labour; fetal wellbeing; 10
Artificial rupture of membranes; pelvic adequacy; 9
Cervical ripening only; cervical length; 12
questions.exp: IOL = initiation of contractions in a patient not in labour; Bishop score assesses cervix/uterus readiness; maximum 13. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Match the mnemonic 'Delhi Police Employed Special Commanders' to Bishop parameters:
opts: Dilation, Position, Effacement, Station, Consistency
Descent, Presentation, Engagement, Show, Contractions
Dilation, Presentation, Effacement, Softness, Cervix length
Duration, Position, Effacement, Station, Colour
questions.exp: Delhi = dilation, Police = position, Employed = effacement, Special = station, Commanders = consistency. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for DILATION of cervix (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):
opts: Closed : 1–2 cm : 3–4 cm : >5 cm
Closed : 1 cm : 2 cm : 3 cm
questions.exp: Dilation: closed 0; 1–2 cm 1; 3–4 cm 2; >5 cm 3 – the most important parameter. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for POSITION of cervix (0 : 1 : 2) and its importance:
opts: Posterior : middle : anterior; least important parameter
Anterior : middle : posterior; most important
Posterior : anterior : middle; moderate
Middle : posterior : anterior; least
questions.exp: Position: posterior 0, middle 1, anterior 2; least important parameter. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for EFFACEMENT (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for STATION of fetal head (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):
opts: Above −2 : −2 : −1, 0 : below ischial spine
Floating : fixed : engaged : crowning
questions.exp: Station: above −2 = 0; −2 = 1; −1/0 = 2; below ischial spine = 3. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Scoring for CONSISTENCY (0 : 1 : 2):
opts: Firm : mid : soft
Soft : mid : firm
Hard : soft : mid
Firm : soft : mid
questions.exp: Consistency: firm 0, mid 1, soft 2. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: The simplified Bishop score uses ______ with a maximum of ______; the modified Bishop score replaces ______ with ______.
opts: Dilation, effacement, station; 9; placement (position) of cervix; length of cervix by USG
Dilation, position, consistency; 7; station; fetal weight
Effacement, station; 6; consistency; cervical length
Dilation, consistency; 5; position; funnelling
questions.exp: Simplified: dilation + effacement + station (max 9). Modified: position replaced by USG cervical length. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Interpretation of the Bishop score — 5 or less : 6 or more : 9 or more.
opts: 5 or less: unripe and induction likely to fail — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: like spontaneous labour
5 or less: favourable — 6 or more: unripe — 9 or more: induction has already failed
5 or less: unripe — 6 or more: still unripe — 9 or more: favourable for induction
5 or less: vaginal delivery certain — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: unripe
questions.exp: A score of 5 or less predicts a failed induction, 6 or more is favourable, and 9 or more behaves like spontaneous labour. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Induction of labour: Bishop score
questions.q: Fill up: A Bishop score of ______ or more predicts a favourable induction, whereas a score of ______ or less means the cervix needs ripening first.
questions.exp: The score combines dilatation, effacement, station, consistency and position; a low score needs prostaglandin or mechanical ripening. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Match the methods – Cervical ripening : IOL : Augmentation.
opts: Ripening: sweeping, mechanical, prostaglandins; IOL: mechanical, PG, oxytocin; augmentation: oxytocin, ARM
Ripening: oxytocin and ARM; IOL: sweeping of membranes; augmentation: prostaglandins
Ripening: prostaglandins only; IOL: ARM only; augmentation: oxytocin only
Ripening: mechanical methods; IOL: sweeping only; augmentation: prostaglandins
questions.exp: Cervical ripening uses sweeping of membranes, mechanical methods and prostaglandins; induction of labour uses mechanical methods, prostaglandins and oxytocin; augmentation uses oxytocin and ARM. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Sweeping (stripping) of membranes – indication and principle:
opts: Slightly dilated cervix; detaching membranes releases prostaglandins and ripens
Closed cervix; stretching the membranes releases oxytocin and ripens
A fully effaced cervix; sweeping deliberately ruptures the membranes
Any cervical state; sweeping mechanically dilates the cervical canal
questions.exp: Sweeping (stripping) of membranes is done when the cervix is slightly dilated; detaching the membranes from the cervix releases prostaglandins and ripens it. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Mechanical methods of IOL both ripen the cervix and induce labour; they are preferred in:
opts: Scarred uterus
Placenta previa
Active genital herpes
Fetal distress
questions.exp: Mechanical methods ripen + induce and are preferred in a scarred uterus. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Transcervical Foley catheter for IOL – size, placement and volume:
opts: A 16 F catheter in the endocervical canal with the bulb at the internal os, inflated with 30 mL saline
A 12 F catheter in the vagina with the bulb at the external os, inflated with 10 mL
A 20 F catheter passed into the uterine cavity and inflated with 60 mL
A 16 F catheter left in the posterior fornix and inflated with 50 mL
questions.exp: The bulb sits at the internal os and is inflated with 30 mL, stretching the cervix and stimulating prostaglandin release. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Extra-amniotic saline infusion (EASI) involves:
opts: Foley through the cervix, bulb inflated, saline infused extra-amniotically
Saline infused into the amniotic cavity through an amniocentesis needle
Saline infused into the bladder to compress the lower uterine segment
Intravenous saline with oxytocin running through the same catheter
questions.exp: EASI places a Foley in the endocervical canal, inflates the bulb and infuses normal saline at 30-40 ml/hr; the saline collects in the extra-amniotic space, separates the membranes and releases prostaglandins. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Hygroscopic dilators used for IOL are exemplified by:
opts: Laminaria tent
Hegar dilator
Karman cannula
Cervidil insert
questions.exp: Hygroscopic dilator = laminaria tent. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
questions.q: Match the method of induction with its description — 1) Membrane sweeping 2) Foley catheter with extra-amniotic saline infusion 3) Intracervical prostaglandin … A) A mechanical method that dilates the cervix and stimulates endogenous prostaglandin release B) A pharmacological ripening agent that also works when membranes have already ruptured C) A simple outpatient method that reduces the need for formal induction but may cause bleeding and discomfort
questions.exp: Sweeping is the simplest, mechanical methods suit women where prostaglandins are risky, and prostaglandins are the pharmacological ripeners. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Prostaglandins for IOL are contraindicated in ______; risk of tachysystole ranks ______.
opts: Scarred uterus; Cervidil > Cerviprime > misoprostol
Primigravida; misoprostol > Cervidil > Cerviprime
Polyhydramnios; Cerviprime > misoprostol > Cervidil
Twins; equal
questions.exp: PG C/I: scarred uterus. Tachysystole: Cervidil > Cerviprime > misoprostol. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Misoprostol (PGE1) for IOL – dose, repetition, maximum and next step:
opts: 25 mcg oral or vaginal 3-6 hourly, max 6 doses; then oxytocin after a gap
50 mcg vaginally 2 hourly, max 4 doses; then caesarean section
100 mcg orally once only; then proceed to an oxytocin infusion
200 mcg vaginally 12 hourly, max 2 doses; then artificial rupture
questions.exp: Misoprostol (PGE1) for induction is 25 mcg oral or vaginal repeated 3-6 hourly (4 hourly), to a maximum of 6 doses; if no labour after a 4 hour gap, move to oxytocin. (Book p521)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Cerviprime gel (dinoprostone PGE2) – dose : site : repeat : maximum : storage.
opts: 0.5 mg : into cervix : 6 hourly : 3 doses, then oxytocin after 6 h : refrigerated
10 mg : posterior fornix : once : 1 : room temperature
0.5 mg : posterior fornix : 12 hourly : 2 : frozen
1 mg : into cervix : 4 hourly : 6 : refrigerated
questions.exp: Cerviprime 0.5 mg intracervical, 6-hourly, max 3 doses (oxytocin 6 h after last), refrigerated. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Cervidil (dinoprostone insert) – dose : release rate : site : duration.
opts: 10 mg : 0.3 mg/hr : posterior fornix : kept 12 h until labour
0.5 mg : 0.1 mg/hr : intracervical : 6 h
25 mcg : 1 mg/hr : vagina : 4 h
5 mg : 0.5 mg/hr : anterior fornix : 24 h
questions.exp: Cervidil 10 mg releasing 0.3 mg/hr, placed in posterior fornix, kept up to 12 h. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Oxytocin for IOL – if cervix is ripe ______; if not ripe ______.
opts: Use oxytocin directly; ripen cervix then oxytocin
Ripen first; oxytocin directly
ARM first; C-section
Misoprostol; Foley
questions.exp: Ripe cervix → oxytocin directly; unripe → ripen then oxytocin. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Standard oxytocin infusion for IOL:
opts: 5 U in 500 ml NS = 10 mIU/ml = 0.5 mIU/drop; max 52 drops/min (26 mIU/min)
10 U in 500 ml = 20 mIU/ml; max 20 drops/min
5 U in 100 ml = 50 mIU/ml; max 10 drops
2 U in 1 L = 2 mIU/ml; max 100 drops
questions.exp: 5 U oxytocin + 500 ml NS → 10 mIU/ml → 0.5 mIU/drop; maximum 52 drops/min = 26 mIU/min. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Side effects of oxytocin infusion:
opts: Water intoxication with hyponatraemia when diluted in dextrose, and hypotension if the rate is too fast
Hypertension with hyperkalaemia from a rapid infusion of the drug
Reflex bradycardia with hyperglycaemia from the accompanying dextrose load
High fever with rigors and hypernatraemia from sodium retention
questions.exp: Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect, so large volumes of 5% dextrose cause hyponatraemia; too rapid a rate causes vasodilatation and hypotension. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
questions.q: Fill up: Vaginal misoprostol for induction is used in low doses of about ______ microgram, and an oxytocin infusion is started at about ______ mU per minute.
questions.exp: Low-dose misoprostol and a low-dose oxytocin infusion that is titrated every 30 minutes minimise uterine hyperstimulation. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL is contraindicated wherever vaginal delivery is contraindicated. Which is NOT on the list?
opts: Previous lower segment C-section
Placenta previa / vasa previa
Malpresentation – transverse lie, brow, mentoposterior face
Active genital herpes / contracted pelvis / CPD / cancer cervix
questions.exp: Listed: placenta previa, vasa previa, malpresentation, active herpes, contracted pelvis, CPD, cancer cervix, previous classical C-section/myomectomy, fetal distress, mono-mono/conjoined twins. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: Which prior surgical histories contraindicate IOL?
opts: Classical C-section and myomectomy
Lower segment C-section and appendicectomy
Cerclage and D&C
Tubal ligation and ovarian cystectomy
questions.exp: Previous classical C-section or myomectomy contraindicate IOL. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: Which twin situations contraindicate IOL?
opts: Monochorionic monoamniotic twins / conjoined twins
Dichorionic diamniotic twins
Both twins cephalic
Twins at 38 weeks
questions.exp: MCMA twins and conjoined twins are C/I to IOL, as is fetal distress. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL in a scarred uterus:
opts: Mechanical method for ripening → oxytocin
Misoprostol 25 mcg → oxytocin
Cervidil insert → ARM
Dinoprostone gel 3 doses
questions.exp: Scarred uterus: mechanical ripening followed by oxytocin (PGs contraindicated). (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: IOL for IUD of fetus – 20–28 weeks : >28 weeks.
opts: 20-28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV, then 400 mcg 3-hourly; over 28 weeks: ripen then oxytocin
20-28 weeks: oxytocin infusion alone; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV 3-hourly
20-28 weeks: mifepristone alone; over 28 weeks: caesarean section in every case
20-28 weeks: misoprostol 25 mcg PV; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 800 mcg 3-hourly
questions.exp: For IUD, at 20-28 weeks give misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV then 400 mcg 3-hourly; beyond 28 weeks give 25 mcg misoprostol to ripen the cervix and then oxytocin. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
questions.q: All of the following are contraindications to induction of labour EXCEPT:
opts: A previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery at term
Placenta previa with the placenta covering the internal os
A previous classical caesarean section with a vertical uterine scar
Cord presentation or vasa previa
questions.exp: An uncomplicated previous vaginal delivery is not a contraindication; anything that obstructs the canal or risks scar rupture or cord compression is. (Book p522)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Third stage of labour – main factor affecting placental separation : plane of separation : m/c method of separation.
opts: Uterine contractions : zona spongiosa : Schultz method
Cord traction : zona basalis : Duncan method
Gravity : zona compacta : Schultz
Maternal pushing : decidua vera : Duncan
questions.exp: Separation depends on uterine contractions, occurs through zona spongiosa, m/c Schultz method. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: The surest sign of placental separation is:
opts: The placenta being felt in the vagina, with apparent permanent lengthening of the cord
A sudden gush of blood before the placenta appears at the introitus
The fundus becoming globular and firm on abdominal palpation
The uterus rising higher in the abdomen above the umbilicus
questions.exp: Feeling the placenta in the vagina, with the cord appearing to lengthen permanently, is the surest sign that separation has occurred. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Passive management of the third stage (not preferred) involves:
opts: Waiting for spontaneous separation and expulsion, with more blood loss and a higher risk of PPH
A uterotonic within one minute of the birth, followed by controlled cord traction
Controlled cord traction with suprapubic counter-pressure and early clamping of the cord
Early cord clamping with immediate traction on the cord to hasten separation of the placenta
questions.exp: Passive management means waiting for signs of separation without a uterotonic; it increases blood loss, PPH and maternal mortality. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Advantages and drawback of AMTSL:
opts: Shortens the third stage, reduces blood loss and prevents PPH, but slightly raises the chance of retained placenta
Lengthens the third stage but reduces PPH; the drawback is uterine inversion
Reduces blood loss only, with neonatal anaemia as its drawback
Prevents retained placenta entirely, but at the cost of more PPH
questions.exp: Active management shortens and de-bloods the third stage, at the price of a small increase in retained placenta from early uterotonics. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
questions.q: Arrange the four steps of AMTSL:
opts: Uterotonic within one minute, delayed cord clamping, controlled cord traction, then intermittent assessment of uterine tone
Cord traction first, then the uterotonic, then clamping, then uterine massage
Early cord clamping, then the uterotonic, then traction, then assessment of tone
Uterine massage first, then the uterotonic, then traction, then late clamping
questions.exp: The four steps run: uterotonic, delayed clamping, controlled cord traction with counter-pressure, then regular assessment of the uterus. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Third stage of labour & active management
questions.q: Match the component of active management with its purpose — 1) Uterotonic within one minute of birth 2) Controlled cord traction 3) Delayed cord clamping … A) The single most effective step for preventing postpartum haemorrhage B) Shortens the third stage when combined with suprapubic counter-pressure, while guarding against cord avulsion C) Allows placental transfusion for 1-3 minutes and improves neonatal iron stores
questions.exp: Active management of the third stage is a package: uterotonic, traction with counter-pressure, and delayed clamping when the baby is well. (Book p523)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: WHO-recommended uterotonic for AMTSL – dose, route, storage:
opts: Oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV infusion (in RL/NS); stored at 2–8 °C
Oxytocin 5 IU IV bolus; room temperature
Methylergometrine 0.2 mg IV; refrigerated
Carboprost 250 mcg IM; room temperature
questions.exp: Oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV infusion; stored 2–8 °C. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Oxytocin IV bolus is contraindicated because it causes ______; 5% dextrose preparation causes ______.
opts: Hypotension, tachycardia and arrhythmias; and water intoxication from its antidiuretic effect
Severe hypertension with intracranial haemorrhage; and hyperglycaemia
Reflex bradycardia with heart block; and hypernatraemia from the salt load
High fever with rigors; and hypokalaemia from intracellular shift
questions.exp: An intravenous bolus of oxytocin causes hypotension and arrhythmias, and large volumes of 5% dextrose cause water intoxication. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: If oxytocin is unavailable, methylergometrine is given as:
opts: 0.2 mg intramuscularly, since the intravenous route can cause severe hypertension
0.5 mg intravenously, with the ampoules kept refrigerated
0.2 mg intravenously, from ampoules that have been stored frozen
1 mg by mouth, stored at room temperature
questions.exp: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg is given intramuscularly; the intravenous route risks a dangerous rise in blood pressure. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Syntometrine is a fixed combination of ______ with the advantage of ______ but disadvantage of ______.
opts: 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg methylergometrine; ↑ efficacy; expensive and ↓ availability
10 U oxytocin + 0.2 mg ME; cheap; hypertension
5 U oxytocin + 250 mcg carboprost; long action; bronchospasm
0.5 mg ME + 600 mcg misoprostol; oral; fever
questions.exp: Syntometrine = 5 U oxytocin + 0.5 mg ME; more efficacious but expensive/less available. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Carbetocin (synthetic oxytocin octapeptide) – dose, half-life and restriction:
opts: 100 microgram slowly intravenously; half-life 40 minutes; not used for induction or for treating PPH
250 microgram intramuscularly; half-life 5 minutes; used to treat PPH
10 IU intramuscularly; half-life 20 minutes; used for induction of labour
1 mg intravenously; half-life 60 minutes; the standard treatment for PPH
questions.exp: Carbetocin is a long-acting oxytocin analogue given as 100 microgram for prevention at caesarean, not for induction or PPH treatment. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Misoprostol (PGE1) as a uterotonic in AMTSL is dosed:
opts: 600 microgram orally or sublingually, within a range of 400 to 600 microgram
25 microgram vaginally, repeated every six hours as required
800 microgram rectally, which is the WHO recommended single dose
200 microgram orally, which is the maximum dose the mother tolerates
questions.exp: In active management misoprostol is used where oxytocin is unavailable, in a dose of 400-600 microgram orally or sublingually. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Type of uterine contraction produced — oxytocin : methylergometrine.
opts: Oxytocin: physiological, with relaxation between contractions — methylergometrine: tetanic, without relaxation
Oxytocin: tetanic, without relaxation between contractions — methylergometrine: physiological, with relaxation
Both drugs produce a tetanic contraction of the uterus that does not relax at all
Both drugs produce physiological contractions with complete relaxation between them
questions.exp: Oxytocin produces physiological contractions with relaxation, whereas ergometrine produces a sustained tetanic contraction and is unsafe before delivery. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Site of action and use – oxytocin : methylergometrine.
opts: Oxytocin acts on both segments and is used for induction and AMTSL; ergometrine is only used after delivery
Oxytocin acts on the lower segment alone and is used for PPH; ergometrine induces labour
Oxytocin acts on the upper segment alone and is used for induction; ergometrine is first line for induction
Oxytocin ripens the cervix; ergometrine acts on the fundus and is used for augmentation
questions.exp: Oxytocin acts on the whole uterus and is used before and after delivery; ergometrine is used only after the baby is born. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Complication – oxytocin : methylergometrine.
opts: Hypotension (with IV bolus) : hypertension
Hypertension : hypotension
Bradycardia : fever
Fever : bronchospasm
questions.exp: Oxytocin bolus → hypotension; ME → hypertension. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Fill up: Oxytocin 10 IU is the first-line uterotonic, while carboprost (15-methyl prostaglandin F2 alpha) is given as ______ microgram and must be avoided in ______.
opts: 250; asthma
125; hypertension
250; diabetes mellitus
500; epilepsy
questions.exp: Carboprost 250 microgram every 15 minutes up to eight doses is second line, but it can provoke severe bronchospasm in asthmatics. (Book p524)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Carboprost/dinoprostone (PGF2α) and tranexamic acid in the third stage are:
opts: Not used in active management; tranexamic acid 1 g is added only when the risk of PPH is high
Both are first-line drugs of active management of the third stage in every delivery
Both are used only for induction of labour and never in the third stage or PPH
Both are contraindicated in the management of established postpartum haemorrhage
questions.exp: Prostaglandins are reserved for treating PPH rather than preventing it, and tranexamic acid is an adjunct where the risk is high. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
questions.q: Dinoprostone (PGE2) is used for ______ but is NOT recommended by WHO for ______.
opts: Induction and augmentation of labour; not for AMTSL or PPH management
Postpartum hemorrhage; not recommended for induction of labour
Active management of the third stage; not for induction
Cervical ripening only; not recommended for augmentation
questions.exp: Dinoprostone (PGE2) is used for induction and augmentation of labour, but WHO does not recommend it for AMTSL or PPH management. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) means clamping at ______ and is included in ______.
opts: ≥1 min (1–3 min); Anemia Mukt Bharat programme
≥30 sec; JSSK
≥5 min; RMNCH+A
After placental delivery; PMSMA
questions.exp: DCC ≥1 min (1–3 min), part of Anemia Mukt Bharat. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Advantage of DCC:
opts: About 80 mL more cord blood reaching the baby, giving extra iron and less neonatal anaemia
Prevention of postpartum haemorrhage in the mother after delivery
A lower risk of neonatal jaundice needing treatment with phototherapy
Prevention of retained placenta in the third stage of labour
questions.exp: Delayed clamping transfers about 80 mL more blood, roughly 50 mg of elemental iron, and reduces infant anaemia; it slightly increases jaundice. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Absolute indication for early cord clamping (ECC):
opts: The need for neonatal resuscitation, as in birth asphyxia
An Rh-negative mother, to limit feto-maternal transfusion
Maternal HIV infection, to reduce the risk of viral transmission
Preterm delivery, to allow immediate paediatric assessment
questions.exp: Clamping is only brought forward when the baby needs resuscitation; otherwise delayed clamping is recommended, including in preterm births. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Relative indications for ECC include all EXCEPT:
opts: Maternal COVID-19 infection
Rh-negative mother with negative ICT (if ICT positive → DCC)
Known heart disease in baby (overload)
Excessive maternal bleeding
questions.exp: Relative ECC: Rh-negative mother ± ICT negative, fetal heart disease, excessive maternal bleeding. COVID-19 is an indication FOR DCC. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: HIV-positive mothers – WHO/ACOG : national guidelines; and what reduces vertical transmission more?
opts: WHO and ACOG advise delayed clamping; national guidance advises clamping once pulsation ceases; antiretrovirals matter more than timing
WHO advises early clamping and national guidance delayed clamping, with early clamping more protective
Both advise delayed clamping, and clamping timing matters more than antiretroviral therapy
Both advise early clamping, and early clamping reduces transmission more than antiretrovirals
questions.exp: Delayed clamping is advised for HIV-positive mothers because transmission is driven by viral load, which antiretroviral therapy controls. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
questions.q: Which of the following statements about delayed cord clamping is TRUE?
opts: It is delayed for at least one to three minutes in babies who do not need resuscitation, and it does not raise the risk of postpartum haemorrhage
The cord must be clamped immediately in every birth to prevent postpartum haemorrhage
Delayed clamping is contraindicated in all preterm infants
Delayed clamping means waiting half an hour before clamping the cord
questions.exp: Delayed clamping improves neonatal iron stores and is especially valuable in preterm babies; it is combined with, not a substitute for, a uterotonic. (Book p525)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Step 3 of AMTSL uses the technique of ______ (a.k.a. ______) performed by ______.
opts: Controlled cord traction; modified Brandt-Andrews technique; skilled birth attendant
Credé's method; fundal expression; any attendant
Manual removal; Johnson's method; obstetrician
Fundal pressure; Kristeller; nurse
questions.exp: CCT = modified Brandt-Andrews technique, by a skilled birth attendant; Credé's method is outdated. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Correct procedure of controlled cord traction:
opts: Wait for separation signs, push the uterus up, then pull the cord forward during a contraction
Pull on the cord continuously from delivery, regardless of any signs of separation
Squeeze the fundus (Credé manoeuvre) while pulling the cord downwards firmly
Apply traction between contractions while an assistant presses on the fundus
questions.exp: Controlled cord traction: look for signs of separation, push the uterus upwards with one hand, then apply gentle downward-forward traction on the cord during a contraction. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: If the cord breaks during CCT, management is:
opts: Manual removal under anaesthesia, sweeping the hand in the plane between the uterus and the placenta
Wait one hour for spontaneous expulsion before any intervention
An oxytocin bolus combined with firm fundal pressure
Emergency hysterectomy, since the cord can no longer be secured
questions.exp: Once the cord snaps, controlled traction is impossible, so the placenta is removed manually in the correct plane under anaesthesia. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Pulling the cord before the placenta has separated risks ______; failure to find a plane between placenta and uterus suggests ______.
opts: Uterine inversion; morbidly adherent placenta (placenta accreta spectrum)
PPH; succenturiate lobe
Cord avulsion; retained membranes
Amniotic fluid embolism; bilobate placenta
questions.exp: Premature traction → uterine inversion; no cleavage plane → placenta accreta spectrum. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Persistent bleeding after placental delivery with a retained part of placenta on USG suggests:
opts: Placenta succenturiata / placenta bilobata
Placenta previa
Vasa previa
Circumvallate placenta
questions.exp: Retained lobe → placenta succenturiata or bilobata. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Step 4 – intermittent assessment of uterine tone is done every ______ for ______; retained placenta/prolonged third stage is defined as placenta undelivered ______ after birth.
opts: 15 min; 1–2 hrs; ≥30 min
5 min; 30 min; ≥15 min
30 min; 4 hrs; ≥60 min
10 min; 1 hr; ≥45 min
questions.exp: Tone every 15 min for 1–2 h; retained placenta = not delivered ≥30 min after baby. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction & the fourth stage
questions.q: Thirty minutes after a normal delivery the placenta is still undelivered, there is no bleeding and the uterus is well contracted. What is the diagnosis and next step?
opts: Retained placenta without haemorrhage — empty the bladder, wait up to 60 minutes and prepare for manual removal if it is still retained
Immediate manual removal of the placenta under general anaesthesia
Emergency hysterectomy, because this must be placenta accreta
Give ergometrine and apply strong traction to the cord to pull the placenta out
questions.exp: Without bleeding the third stage may safely be allowed up to an hour; traction beyond control risks cord avulsion and uterine inversion. (Book p526)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Fourth stage of labour – duration, a normal maternal experience and monitoring intervals:
opts: One to two hours after the placenta; physiological chills; observations every 15 minutes
Twenty-four hours after delivery; fever; vital signs taken hourly throughout
Thirty minutes after delivery; rigors; vital signs taken every five minutes
Six hours after delivery; sweating; vital signs taken every half hour
questions.exp: The fourth stage is the first one to two hours after delivery, when the woman may shiver and needs close observation. (Book p527)

questions.sec: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
questions.q: Advice given in the fourth stage and its possible complications:
opts: Pass urine and take oral fluids within 2 hours; watch for PPH, tears, hematoma
Remain nil by mouth for a full 6 hours; watch for uterine rupture
Strict bed rest for 24 hours after delivery; watch for deep vein thrombosis
Keep the catheter in place for 12 hours; watch for postpartum infection
questions.exp: In the fourth stage the mother is advised to pass urine and take oral intake within 2 hours of delivery; the complications to watch for are PPH, perineal tears and vulval hematoma. (Book p527)

units.title: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
units.guide: Define normal labour by its five criteria and walk through the four uterine phases from quiescence to postpartum with their hormonal drivers. Focus for this checkpoint: Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour.

units.title: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
units.guide: Recognise lightening, false pains and the biochemistry of cervical ripening, then separate true from false labour pain across six features. Focus for this checkpoint: Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain.

units.title: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
units.guide: Quantify the origin, speed, pressure thresholds and stage-wise strengths of contractions, and understand Montevideo units and segment formation. Focus for this checkpoint: The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions.

units.title: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions
units.guide: Define tachysystole and precipitate labour with their causes and consequences, and manage hypertonic and hypotonic uterine activity. Focus for this checkpoint: Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions.

units.title: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence
units.guide: Identify Kocher's forceps, the prostaglandin logic of ARM, its absolute and relative contraindications, and the engaged/unengaged sequencing rule. Focus for this checkpoint: Augmentation of labour: ARM & sequence.

units.title: Cardinal movements & the process of labour
units.guide: Order the seven cardinal movements and know the degree of rotation, the definition of crowning, restitution and WHO perineal protection steps. Focus for this checkpoint: Cardinal movements & the process of labour.

units.title: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters
units.guide: Define engagement by the biparietal diameter, its clinical signs, why a primigravida's head may float at term and which AP diameter engages in each attitude. Focus for this checkpoint: Engagement: definition, signs, causes of non-engagement & engaging diameters.

units.title: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement
units.guide: Distinguish synclitic from anterior and posterior asynclitic engagement by where the sagittal suture points, and recall how the head is delivered in vertex vs breech/face. Focus for this checkpoint: Synclitic & asynclitic engagement.

units.title: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
units.guide: Trace the spinal segments carrying 1st and 2nd stage pain, and set the level, drugs, effects, monitoring and contraindication of epidural analgesia. Focus for this checkpoint: Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia.

units.title: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins
units.guide: Locate the pudendal and paracervical block sites, their uses and hazards, then cover prostaglandin receptors, synthesis sites and obstetric uses. Focus for this checkpoint: Pudendal & paracervical blocks and prostaglandins.

units.title: Induction of labour: Bishop score
units.guide: Score every Bishop parameter with the DELHI POLICE mnemonic, know the most and least important items, the simplified and modified versions, and interpret the totals. Focus for this checkpoint: Induction of labour: Bishop score.

units.title: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
units.guide: Group the ripening, induction and augmentation methods, then detail membrane sweeping, Foley, EASI and laminaria – the options preferred in a scarred uterus. Focus for this checkpoint: Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods.

units.title: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction
units.guide: Dose misoprostol, cerviprime gel and Cervidil correctly, rank their tachysystole risk, and prepare and titrate oxytocin safely. Focus for this checkpoint: Prostaglandins & oxytocin for induction.

units.title: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases
units.guide: Recall the ten conditions where vaginal delivery – and hence induction – is contraindicated, and the protocols for scarred uterus and intrauterine death. Focus for this checkpoint: Contraindications to IOL & IOL in special cases.

units.title: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview
units.guide: Master placental separation physiology, the signs, passive vs active management and the four steps of AMTSL. Focus for this checkpoint: Third stage of labour & AMTSL overview.

units.title: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives
units.guide: Dose and store oxytocin, methylergometrine, syntometrine, carboprost and misoprostol, and contrast oxytocin with methylergometrine. Focus for this checkpoint: Step 1: uterotonics – oxytocin & alternatives.

units.title: Step 2: delayed cord clamping
units.guide: Time delayed clamping, its iron benefit and programme link, and list every absolute and relative indication for early clamping including the HIV nuance. Focus for this checkpoint: Step 2: delayed cord clamping.

units.title: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage
units.guide: Perform controlled cord traction correctly, handle the special cases (cord snap, inversion, PAS, succenturiate lobe), then run fourth-stage monitoring. Focus for this checkpoint: Steps 3 & 4: controlled cord traction, special cases & fourth stage.
